# What is in the findings files

<!-- Generated by `python3 research/tools/check.py --index`. Do not edit by
     hand: `check.py` fails when this file and the findings disagree. -->

77 files, 29.6 MB, 15,230 findings.

**Never read one whole.** The largest,
`sf-context-statements/umb-survey-ratings.json`, is 4.1 MB — about 1.1M
tokens, more than a context window holds. The directory as a whole is around
7.8M tokens, and an agent that opens one of these files has usually spent
its session to reach three entries.

This file is the cheap way in. The table says what each batch covers;
the commands below get entries out without the file entering the context.

## Getting entries out

```bash
# what a batch is, what it covered, and a sample of its entries
python3 research/tools/check.py --peek research/findings/<id>/<batch>.json

# every entry matching some words, across every file (or one of them)
python3 research/tools/check.py --find "1377 Fulton"
python3 research/tools/check.py --find Fulton --in research/findings/digitalsf/sfp-23.json
```

For anything those two don't answer, query the file rather than opening
it — `jq` on the entries, never `cat` on the file:

```bash
jq '.findings[] | select(.street_name == "FULTON") | {id, address_as_written, description}' <file>
jq '[.findings[] | select(.resolution.status == "unresolved")] | length' <file>
jq -r '.findings[] | select(.publish.status == "published") | .resolution.path' <file> | sort -u
```

## The shape, once

Every file is the same object, so it is written down here rather than
discovered by reading one:

```
{ source_id, batch, read_on, notes, coverage: { unit, examined, remaining,
  mentions, note }, findings: [ … ] }
```

An entry, with the share of the 15,230 that carry each key:

| key | on |
|---|---:|
| `address_as_written` | 100% |
| `citation` | 100% |
| `date` | 100% |
| `description` | 100% |
| `id` | 100% |
| `kind` | 100% |
| `resolution` | 100% |
| `date_precision` | 99% |
| `street_name` | 98% |
| `street_number` | 96% |
| `street_type` | 92% |
| `extra` | 92% |
| `raw` | 91% |
| `publish` | 86% |
| `confidence` | 79% |
| `conflict` | 5% |
| `note` | 0% |

`resolution` is `{status, apn, path, eas_address, method, checked_on, note}`
and `publish` is `{status, pr, note}`. Every field and its rules:
[../schema/finding.schema.json](../schema/finding.schema.json).
